The Samsung Galaxy Z Flip launched to much fanfare in February 2020. Dubbed as the third "mass-market" foldable smartphone, this folding phone flipped (quite literally) the display into a clamshell design reminiscent of retro flip phones as well as the newly updated Motorola RAZR foldable. Unlike the Moto, however, Samsung packed some seriously good specs into this handset. You get a 1080p equivalent ultra-wide 21.9:9 1080p-equivalent display, a Snapdragon 855+, 8GB, 256GB+ storage, and all a camera assembly similar to that found in the Galaxy S10. Sure, there have been early reports of durability issues from fellow YouTubers like JerryRigEverything, but we believe they're largely blown out of proportion and whilst Samsung should be chastised for misleading advertising, the glass display is *actually* glass and is *actually* really great. The question, however, remains: "Is this phone worth $1,400?" and "Can the Galaxy Z Flip with 2019 specs really hold a candle to Samsung's 2020 flagship Galaxy S20 line?" In a way, yes. In other ways, no. One thing is to be sure: this thing is made of glass, it folds, and it's actually really great. #SnazzyLabs #Samsung #GalaxyZFlip

Snazzy Labs makes a case for a smaller, modular Mac; a Mac Pro mini. The Mac Pro is great and all, but its $6,000 starting price point and "one-size-fits-all-pros" approach means its financially out of reach for many of us mere mortals. But rather than turn to hackintosh land, why couldn't Apple just make a smaller ATX or mini-ITX sized Mac Pro mini—one with the same upgradable RAM, CPU, GPU, and more for less money and in a smaller case? Snazzy Labs takes a look at the new NZXT H1 mini-ITX SFF case. With a built-in AIO, SFF PSU, and PCIe riser card for the GPU, this case is ready to rumble from the factory. Just insert your mini ITX motherboard, attach the cooler, plug-in the pre-wired cables and insert your GPU. That's it. You're done. The whole build takes less than 10 minutes. Pretty freaking awesome for what are historically nightmarish cases to build in.

snippet.description:
The 2019 Mac Pro has been lauded by many as the end-all-be-all of video editing workstations. But that's only if you have big $$$. We put Linux on our AMD Ryzen 3950X PC and see how it holds up.

Follow me on Twitter - http://twitter.com/snazzyq
Follow me on Instagram - http://instagram.com/snazzyq

Many tech YouTubers use Final Cut Pro X and Adobe Premiere Pro to edit their videos, but Derek, the cinematographer here at Snazzy Labs uses Blackmagic Davinci Resolve. Unlike the other two popular NLEs, Resolve is available for Mac, Windows, and Linux but was originally developed for Linux to use in a professional studio/post-processing environment. We took our PC rocking a 3950X CPU, a GTX 1080 (ya, we know, we're waiting on the new 2080 Ti Super), and put this thing to the test. Not only does it run Linux, but it does so very well. Running the Debian/Ubuntu-based Pop!_OS, this thing is ready to rumble.

After years of waiting, Tesla has unveiled the new electric pickup truck dubbed Cybertruck. It looks like something straight out of Cyberpunk 2077 with a retro-futuristic design that's... controversial. Is it ugly? Is it beautiful? Is it in the eye of the beholder? snippet.title: Apple and Intel Are Breaking Up
snippet.description:
AMD is ready to dethrone Intel, but Apple doesn't care. Why? They're making their own ARM chips and leaving both behind. Let's talk about it.

Follow me on Twitter - http://twitter.com/snazzyq
Follow me on Instagram - http://instagram.com/snazzyq

Apple has undergone a number of transitions in the past. In the early 90s, they moved from Motorola's 68k platform to IBM's PowerPC architecture. For a few years, Apple made the fastest personal computers on the planet. But PowerPC had a number of issues and Apple was forced to move to Intel in the mid 2000s. It was a good transition and helped the Mac a lot, but it's now time for Apple to transition once again leaving Intel, AMD, and the x86 architecture in the dust. Hello, ARM. The new Apple-made custom chips for Mac could be a game-changer and could make Apple exciting again. Battery life would improve, thermal throttling could disappear, and the chips could obliterate the competition thanks to application-specific hardware and a software stack to match.

At the time of this video, there is no updated guide for the 2017 iMac; however, it's very similar to the 2014-2015 A1419 model. The only big difference is the screw placement on the motherboard. I bent the CPU back (silicon bends easily without damaging, luckily), reinserted it into the socket, and was more careful when I tightened the CPU cooler the second time. It's easy to wiggle the CPU out of place when installing the cooler, so be careful—and if it feels too hard to tighten the CPU socket, stop—something is wrong.

snippet.title: Let's Talk about Ads on Snazzy Labs
snippet.description:
Let’s talk about ads on Snazzy Labs. I started this channel nearly 9-years-ago. What started as a hobby has become a near full-time job which I’m incredibly grateful for. Being able to make money doing something I love and am passionate about is awesome. But not only am I a creator—I’m also a viewer of a lot of other channels. I’ve been in your shoes. And I know how much ads can suck. The purpose of this video is to help to find an equilibrium—where you don’t hate the ads I do when I have to do them, where the brands I work with are happy with the results, and where I’m able to continue YouTubing as a career and grow my channel even further.

Why do I have to do ads in the first place? Doesn’t YouTube pay enough? No. Google is continuing to pay it’s creators less and less money. Last month, my channel got 4x the amount of views that it did in the same month of last year, but I got paid about the same amount—so YouTube is paying 4 times less than they did last year. Many YouTube Creators have come to rely on platforms like Patreon—where the audience pays the creator. Maybe that works for them, but I’m not comfortable with that. Ads are a far better solution. They pay way more money, and so I can do them less often. Right now, I only have ads on about 1 in 5 videos. If I moved to Patreon, I’d have to beg for money at the beginning and ending of every single video to match what advertisers are paying me now. YouTube is a free platform, and you shouldn’t be expected or guilt-tripped into supporting me financially when brands are so anxious to advertise on my channel.

At the same time, I refuse to let the premium quality content I make, be watered down and cheapened by crappy ads. Here are the promises I make to you as a viewer:

1. I will only ever work with brands whose product I use and love—I get emails every single day offering a LOT of money to sponsor or advertise on videos—and I say no to nearly all of them because I will never advertise for crappy services or products because that’s not fair to you—to be told something is good when it isn’t.

2. Brands are not allowed to alter or change my ad integration. A lot of you didn’t like the Privacy ad from my last video. It was a 4 minute ad in an 8 minute video. If I could go back in time, I’d do it shorter. I apologize. But the ad wasn’t 4 minutes because Privacy said so, or because it was in the contract. It was 4 minutes because I really genuinely love the service and wanted to demo all of its cool features. I don’t allow brands to dictate how I make my videos. I apologize for the super long ad, I’ll exercise more self-restraint, and it won’t happen again.

3. I will NEVER do a paid review. I will always verbally state in the video, and disclose in the video description if a product is sponsored. Furthermore, I pride myself on journalistic integrity and will not provide special treatment to brands that have advertised with Snazzy Labs in the past.

4. I will NOT do fully-sponsored videos—because those are B.S. For example, Wix, the website building software company, paid a ton of YouTubers a LOT of money last year to make an entire video about their service. And no offense to the YouTubers that accepted, but I said no. Not only because I don’t think Wix is a very good service, but because videos where the whole thing is an ad are not genuine, they cheapen my brand, and most importantly, they’re not fair to YOU as a viewer. That’s not the content you subscribed for.

5. I will only advertise when by doing so, I can continue to provide unique, non-clickbait, and high-budget videos that would not be possible without support from advertisers. I have an incredibly cool video next week that—spoiler alert—is sponsored, but it’s a very expensive project that would not have been possible otherwise. And it’s a freaking cool video that’s well-worth sitting through a short little ad.

I don’t pretend to have all the answers on the best way to advertise—given the negative feedback from my last video—it’s apparent I still have a lot to learn and experiment with, so I’d love to hear your thoughts on the types of advertisements you’ve seen on both this channel and other channels that you’ve either liked or hated and provide suggestions in the comment section below for how I can continue to make Snazzy Labs videos the most unique tech videos on the Net. Thanks so much for watching, thank you millions for your support, and as always, stay snazzy.

FlexPlay was one of the more interesting takes on temporary disposable DVD rentals. Circuit City tried its own DIVX which multi-million dollar failure due to ridiculous DRM standards and the necessity for a phone line for verification. Unfortunately, due to the strong-arm Blockbuster corporation and other limitations such as shelf life and price, Flexplay became one of the larger product failures of the last decade.

snippet.title: Final Quinn Update! (March 2014)
snippet.description:
My dearest Snazzy Labs audience,

As I write this letter, I realize that it is my last that you will receive.  In a few very short months, I will return to the United States and the world of tech.  My experience here with the people of Bolivia has been unparalleled.  I have met and had the opportunity to help close to 1,000 people and I have made friends that will last a lifetime.

Upon my arrival, I will jump back into my routine of making great tech videos.  I have bought a Macbook Air and iPad mini Retina which are awating my arrival.  Obviously, to make tech vids once again, I will need better equipment than what awaits me: good cameras, microphones, a desktop computer, etc.

That is where I need your help.

Imagine having left to a 3rd world country two years ago and not having heard nor seen basically anything about modern tech.  That is where I am at right now.  When I left:

The lastest and greatest iPhone was a 4S (with that tiny little 3.5" screen) running iOS 5.
The "new iPad" retina (3rd generation) was brand spanking new.
The iPad mini didn't exist yet.
The MacBook Pro didn't have a retina model yet and used Ivy Bridge processors.
The parallax website phenom didn't exist yet.
Apple still gave out the lousy in-ear headphones with their devices.
Ice Cream Sandwich was the latest version of Android.
I was skinny.  A few of you have seen that I gained a little... well a lot of weight.  LOL.  But Bolivian food is good!  I will be skinny when I get back.
Much has changed without my knowledge.  Upon my arrival, I commit to read 2 years of tech news, try-out new devices, basically everything that will be necessary for me to be the Snazzy guy filled with knowledge that I once was.

The first video you will see from me will come on May 12.  It will be a friendly welcome-back video with a few exciting announcements. I will also announce an important meeting: "Snazzy Town Hall" which will be a live stream on May 17th.  Together, we will decide the future horizon of Snazzy Labs.

I thank each and every one of you for your amazing loyalty and support these last two years.  I have the best viewers!

As always, and until May, stay snazzy!

Quinn

snippet.title: Quinn Update - November 2013
snippet.description:
Snazzy Labs fans,

 

What a wonderful last several months has it been!  I hope you all have been well.  Here in Bolivia it has been an incredible experience for me and those lifelong friends I have come to know and love.

 

This is a very special time of year -- and not only because it is Thanksgiving season with Christmas around the corner.  On December 8, Snazzy Labs will complete its 5th year anniversary.  It has been an amazing ride.  I started making YouTube videos back in 2008 as a mere hobby to see if anyone would watch.  I recommend you take some time to go back to my first video review of the Bose In-Ear Headphones.  It is terrible!  LOL.  I would have never imagined us to come this far.  We have come a long way since my 3.2 Megapixel Sony CyberShot and iMovie software on my PowerPC iMac G5.   Your love and support has helped me to make over 890 videos which have been viewed millions of times over.

 

2014 will be a very exciting time for Snazzy Labs.  After this video finishes, there will be only one more video update before my arrival back home.  I get back into the good 'ol USA on May 9th.  I will surely need a few weeks to get adjusted to the Gringo-life once again and to play "catch-up" on the two years of tech news that slipped through my fingers.  That's not even mentioning the fact that I sold just about all my gear before I left, so I will need to buy new computers, phones, recording equipment, etc .

 

I am confident that we will see a lot of improvements to the way I generate and publish the content.  I will get to re-designing and constructing all my websites that look "so 2012" and fine tuning that which is de-tuned.  I also hope to further develop ventures that I have already started such as Headphone Mecca.  I am seriously considering making all my content into both English and Spanish to help balance the unfairly English-based tech world.  Be assured that it will stay your classic "snazzy" content you all know and love.

 

I don't know what kind of gear I will have when I get back.  I think I will buy one of the new Mac Pros for video production with a MacBook Air on the side for school and my Netflix cravings.  I think an iPad mini with Retina Display will suit my mobile gaming needs with a Nexus 5 unlocked on T-Mobile until the release of the iPhone 6 in the fall. 

 

Well, that's it for this episode.  I wish you all to have a joyous holiday season with your families and loved ones.  I pray that you'll be able to help those in need and have the true spirit of service.  Thanks so much for your continued support and as always, stay snazzy!

snippet.title: Quinn Update August '13
snippet.description:
Dear those of you that are still left (nah, that is a joke),

It has been a crazy last few months here in Bolivia.  I have moved areas again and am now in the center of Santa Cruz working in the office to help other missionaries with housing, finances, etc.  I went a few days ago to help a poor family cut 1/2 acre of grass with machetes.  My arm hurts writing this.  LOL.  It has been a great experience and the time keeps passing crazy quick!  May 2014 is just around the corner.

In downtown Santa Cruz, it is a lot wealthier, and, going to the office, I see a lot of technology.  I have seen a Samsung Galaxy S4, iPad Mini (I want one!) and the iPhone 5.  The Galaxy S4 is a beautiful telephone and I feel like I would prefer it to the hardware of the iPhone 5.  The screen is pretty!

I heard about the Apple announcement this past week and I have a few comments.  The Mac Pro looks freaking awesome!  I am so happy that Apple didn't kill the machine off.  The redesign looks amazing.  I am left a little skeptical about this thermal core, but if the fan is actually quiet and the unit stays cool I will be stoked.  At the end of 2013 to save face on taxes, I will have to make a few "business expenses," and a Mac Pro will be one of those.  I am a little nervous that they didn't include the price in the preview.  It is going to cost an arm and a leg...  And then another leg.  The most impressive thing to me (after all of the tech specs of course) is the size.  10" tall is crazy tiny!  I am happy to see that Apple still has all of their ridiculously unnecessarily bells and whistles like the I/O panel that lights up when the machine senses motion.  Nonetheless, I am stoked to hear that Apple is not trying to kill the desktop, rather, to integrate desktop and mobile a little more tightly.

That brings me to OS X Mavericks.  I understand that they ran out of cat names, but Mavericks?  That is a super weird name.  It just makes me think of the NBA.  Don't care about iBooks.  Don't care about Maps.  Don't use Calendar.app.  I prefer Chrome to Safari.  Full-screen apps on multiple displays should not be a "new feature," rather something that needed to be included as a bug fix.  Finder tabs is cool.  Tags seem like something I will never use.  All in all, not a big update.  I wonder how far off Mac OS 11 is.

The new MacBook Air update seems nice.  I will be buying one next year for school.  Nobody can complain about better battery.

The AirPort Extreme has always been a lousy router in my mind.  Maybe the new one will change the bad history.

iOS 7 looks interesting.  I am happy that after 5 years they are finally changing the look up.  I love the lighter, whiter style.  It looks very "Windows Phone-esque" if I do say so.  The most pretty is the photo album and iTunes Radio.  The Camera capture button looks kinda out of place.  The new Siri functions make my robot gal look a lot more functional.  I am a little skeptical about this "iOS in the car."   It looks strangely and mysteriously half-baked.  I feel like it is something Steve wouldn't have publicly announced until it was ready for shipment.  That being said, it will be neat if they can convince car manufacturers to change their current setup.  While still loyally committed to Mac, I feel like it will be a tough decision in the mobile game when I get back.

Well, back to work!  Nonetheless, I thank each and every one of you for your continued loyalty.  Only 3 more video updates!  I will be back sooner that you all know it.  I have gotten pretty good at my Spanish, and so I will definitely do my videos in 2 languages upon my return.  Should I make "Snazzy Labs Español" or a whole new network for my Latino audience?  For example like "Gringo Tech."  Send your suggestions and commentaries to my address:

Elder Quinn Nelson
Misión Bolivia Santa Cruz
Casilla de Correo 2042
Zona Central
Santa Cruz, Santa Cruz
Bolivia

As always, stay snazzy!

Quinn

snippet.title: Quinn Update - June '13
snippet.description:
I cannot believe that the months have already passed by so quickly!  It is so good to finally send you all an update.  The work here in Bolivia has been crazy.  I sometimes don't even have time to eat!  I have moved to a new part of Santa Cruz on the north side of the city.  It is really weird here because there is extreme wealth and extreme poverty all in the same neighborhood.  One street has 3 really big mansions and next to them (sometimes even sharing the same wall), is a house made out of wood without running water.  Its a really different world but we all just have to remember that the little help we can give does a lot for other people.

As for technology, I am a little bit more up to date.

I have seen and played with the iPhone 5.  It is a pretty phone but I was seemingly under impressed.  iOS is left basically the same.  My dad who is a huge Apple fan recently made the move to Android on a Galaxy Note 2 and seems to be happy.  When I left, Android was growing fast but still had a ton of scalability problems and lacked polish; however, I wouldn't be surprised to hear that Google has changed up their act.

The other day in the bus, I saw an ASUS laptop tablet running Windows 8.  I was absolutely marveled at the fluidity and beauty of Windows 8; however, yesterday, I used a laptop running Windows 8 and got so frustrated with changing screens and weird bugs I changed to a Windows XP computer.  I am sure it just lacked optimization, but it wasn't very intuitive because I got completely lost.  And I consider myself tech savvy!  I can't even imagine an old lady trying to use that thing...  Nonetheless, it reminded me why I am a Mac user.  LOL.  Speaking of Macs, they basically don't exist here.  I have only seen the iPhone 5 and the new iPod Nano.  In fact, I thought the new iPod Nano was a Chinese knockoff the first time I saw it because of the circular home button logo.  Why did they leave the "squircle" behind?  After playing with the new iPod Nano, I concluded it was the same thing as the last generation.  Just a slightly better form factor.

I haven't seen any of the new Android phones here.  I saw a Sony Xperia smartphone that was really gorgeous.  In fact, it actually surprised me that it was a Sony phone.  They have historically been awful, but it was really pretty.  I don't think it was running the new Android however.  I am pretty sure it was ICS because it looked familiar.

I hope all is well back home and I send you guys all the thanks and love in the world.  Can you believe I have already been gone one whole year?  Time passes by quick!  This time next year and you'll already be watching my videos once again - in English and Spanish.  Thanks for your patience and for being the snazziest fans ever!  In the next few months, I am gonna need your help to let me know what is happening in the tech world for my arrival.  I am going to come back a total n00b!  Don't forget you can send me snail mail and I will try my best to respond!

Elder Quinn Nelson

Santa Cruz, Santa Cruz
Bolivia

As always, stay snazzy!
Quinn

snippet.title: Forgot your Mac Password? Reset it Without Losing Data nor Install Disc (OS X 10.5 and older)
snippet.description:
Have a newer OS?  For those running 10.6 or above, I have created a newer (simpler) video guide - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CJ6AZMk2cy0

Process 1 -

mount -uw /
launchctl load /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.DirectoryServices.plist
ls /Users
dscl . -passwd /Users/username password
reboot

Process 2 - 
mount -uw /
rm /var/db/.AppleSetupDone
shutdown -h now

snippet.title: Terminal Tip Tuesday - Prevent iTunes from Launching While Using Play / FF/ Rew Hotkeys
snippet.description:
Download iTunes.py Script (Open with TextEdit) - http://cl.ly/4JZQ

Terminal Commands (one at a time):

cd /Applications/iTunes.app/Contents/MacOS
sudo mv iTunes iTunesX
sudo mv [path of iTunes.py file]/iTunes.py iTunes
sudo chown root:admin iTunes
sudo chmod 0755 iTunes

--

This is not my code; it was found on the Apple Discussion Forums and I do not take credit for the script creation nor am I to be liable for the modifications it can/will make.
